scenes.tts: What would a synapse need, to store an association?
scenes.visual: Two neurons joined by one synapse, which glows softly. The question appears beside them.
scenes.narration: What would a synapse need, to store an association?

scenes.tts: In 1949, Donald Hebb proposed a rule. When one cell repeatedly helps fire another, the connection between them grows.
scenes.visual: Caption card: Donald Hebb, 1949. Cell A fires and cell B fires just after; the synapse between them thickens.
scenes.narration: In 1949, Donald Hebb proposed a rule. When one cell repeatedly helps fire another, the connection between them grows.

scenes.tts: Treat that as a design specification. The synapse should strengthen when two things happen together.
scenes.visual: A checklist titled Design spec appears with two empty boxes.
scenes.narration: Treat that as a design specification. The synapse should strengthen when two things happen together.

scenes.tts: Its own input is active. And the cell it talks to is active at the same moment.
scenes.visual: The first box ticks as the presynaptic terminal flashes; the second ticks as the postsynaptic cell depolarizes. Labels: input active; postsynaptic cell active (depolarized).
scenes.narration: Its own input is active. And the cell it talks to is active at the same moment.

scenes.tts: First, we need evidence that synapses change at all. Most of it comes from the hippocampus, so here is a map.
scenes.visual: A simplified hippocampus outline fades in, curled like a seahorse.
scenes.narration: First, we need evidence that synapses change at all. Most of it comes from the hippocampus, so here is a map.

scenes.tts: Input arrives from the entorhinal cortex. Its axons, the perforant path, reach the dentate gyrus and its granule cells.
scenes.visual: An arrow labelled perforant path runs from entorhinal cortex to the dentate gyrus; small granule cells light up.
scenes.narration: Input arrives from the entorhinal cortex. Its axons, the perforant path, reach the dentate gyrus and its granule cells.

scenes.tts: The granule cells' axons, the mossy fibres, reach the pyramidal cells of C A three.
scenes.caption: The granule cells' axons, the mossy fibres, reach the pyramidal cells of CA3.
scenes.visual: An arrow labelled mossy fibres runs from dentate gyrus to CA3 pyramidal cells.
scenes.narration: The granule cells' axons, the mossy fibres, reach the pyramidal cells of CA3.

scenes.tts: Their axons, the Schaffer collaterals, reach the pyramidal cells of C A one. Most of this story happens at that last relay.
scenes.caption: Their axons, the Schaffer collaterals, reach the pyramidal cells of CA1. Most of this story happens at that last relay.
scenes.visual: An arrow labelled Schaffer collaterals runs from CA3 to CA1. The three synapses are marked with numbered dots.
scenes.narration: Their axons, the Schaffer collaterals, reach the pyramidal cells of CA1. Most of this story happens at that last relay.

scenes.tts: We will visit three synapses on this chain. The first is where lasting change was first measured.
scenes.visual: Dot 1, perforant path to dentate gyrus, pulses.
scenes.narration: We will visit three synapses on this chain. The first is where lasting change was first measured.

scenes.tts: In 1973, Tim Bliss and Terje Lomo reported it, in anaesthetized rabbits.
scenes.caption: In 1973, Tim Bliss and Terje Lømo reported it, in anaesthetized rabbits.
scenes.visual: Caption card: Bliss and Lømo, 1973, anaesthetized rabbits.
scenes.narration: In 1973, Tim Bliss and Terje Lømo reported it, in anaesthetized rabbits.

scenes.tts: They stimulated the perforant path and recorded from the dentate gyrus, with an electrode outside the cells.
scenes.visual: A stimulating electrode on the perforant path; a recording electrode sits among the granule cells, outside them.
scenes.narration: They stimulated the perforant path and recorded from the dentate gyrus, with an electrode outside the cells.

scenes.tts: That electrode records a field potential: an extracellular voltage made by the summed currents of many neurons.
scenes.visual: Many small cell currents add into one trace on a scope.
scenes.narration: That electrode records a field potential: an extracellular voltage made by the summed currents of many neurons.

scenes.tts: A test pulse gives two parts. A slow wave, the population E P S P, measures synaptic strength.
scenes.caption: A test pulse gives two parts. A slow wave, the population EPSP, measures synaptic strength.
scenes.visual: The trace draws a slow downward wave. Its initial slope is highlighted and labelled field EPSP slope = synaptic strength.
scenes.narration: A test pulse gives two parts. A slow wave, the population EPSP, measures synaptic strength.

scenes.tts: A sharp spike riding on it shows how many cells fire, and how closely in time.
scenes.visual: A sharp notch appears on the wave, labelled population spike = cells firing together.
scenes.narration: A sharp spike riding on it shows how many cells fire, and how closely in time.

scenes.tts: Between test pulses, they gave brief high frequency trains, called a tetanus. One regimen was 100 pulses per second, for 3 to 4 seconds.
scenes.caption: Between test pulses, they gave brief high-frequency trains, called a tetanus. One regimen was 100 pulses per second, for 3 to 4 seconds.
scenes.visual: A dense burst of stimulus ticks. Label: tetanus, 100 per second for 3 to 4 s.
scenes.narration: Between test pulses, they gave brief high-frequency trains, called a tetanus. One regimen was 100 pulses per second, for 3 to 4 seconds.

scenes.tts: Afterwards, the same test pulse gave a larger response, in 15 of 18 rabbits. It lasted from 30 minutes to 10 hours.
scenes.visual: A time-course plot: responses near 100% before the train, then a step up that stays high. On screen: 15 of 18 rabbits; 30 min to 10 h.
scenes.narration: Afterwards, the same test pulse gave a larger response, in 15 of 18 rabbits. It lasted from 30 minutes to 10 hours.

scenes.tts: This lasting rise is long term potentiation, or L T P.
scenes.caption: This lasting rise is long-term potentiation, or LTP.
scenes.visual: The raised plateau is labelled long-term potentiation (LTP).
scenes.narration: This lasting rise is long-term potentiation, or LTP.

scenes.tts: How do you know the change belongs to that input? Record a second pathway to the same cells, and leave it untrained.
scenes.visual: A second, grey pathway joins the same cells. Its time-course line is added to the plot.
scenes.narration: How do you know the change belongs to that input? Record a second pathway to the same cells, and leave it untrained.

scenes.tts: If the preparation were drifting, that pathway would drift too. If it stays flat while the trained one rises, the change is input specific.
scenes.visual: The grey line stays flat near 100% while the trained line rises. Label: input specific.
scenes.narration: If the preparation were drifting, that pathway would drift too. If it stays flat while the trained one rises, the change is input specific.

scenes.tts: In a made up recording, the slope rose to 160 percent of baseline. The spike rose to 250 percent. Is the synapse two and a half times stronger?
scenes.caption: In a made-up recording, the slope rose to 160% of baseline. The spike rose to 250%. Is the synapse two and a half times stronger?
scenes.visual: On screen: EPSP slope 160% of baseline; population spike 250% of baseline. A question mark over the synapse.
scenes.narration: In a made-up recording, the slope rose to 160% of baseline. The spike rose to 250%. Is the synapse two and a half times stronger?

scenes.tts: No. Synaptic strength is read from the slope, and it rose much less.
scenes.visual: The slope value, 160%, is highlighted as the measure of synaptic strength.
scenes.narration: No. Synaptic strength is read from the slope, and it rose much less.

scenes.tts: Firing has a threshold. A modest rise in the E P S P pushes many more cells past it. So the spike grows out of proportion.
scenes.caption: Firing has a threshold. A modest rise in the EPSP pushes many more cells past it. So the spike grows out of proportion.
scenes.visual: A row of cells with a threshold line; a slightly taller EPSP pushes many more cells over it, and the spike bar jumps.
scenes.narration: Firing has a threshold. A modest rise in the EPSP pushes many more cells past it. So the spike grows out of proportion.

scenes.tts: To test whether the cells became more excitable, compare spike size at matched E P S P size.
scenes.caption: To test whether the cells became more excitable, compare spike size at matched EPSP size.
scenes.visual: Two traces with equal EPSP slopes, overlaid; only their spikes are compared.
scenes.narration: To test whether the cells became more excitable, compare spike size at matched EPSP size.

scenes.tts: The record leaves three puzzles. How can a synapse detect that both cells were active together? What decides whether it goes up or down? And does memory use it?
scenes.visual: Three numbered cards: 1 Coincidence, 2 Direction, 3 Memory.
scenes.narration: The record leaves three puzzles. How can a synapse detect that both cells were active together? What decides whether it goes up or down? And does memory use it?

scenes.tts: One receptor answers the first puzzle, and offers a model for the second. At Schaffer collateral to C A one synapses, with normal magnesium outside the cell, L T P is triggered by calcium entering through N M D A receptors. Substantial entry needs glutamate and enough local depolarization together.
scenes.caption: One receptor answers the first puzzle, and offers a model for the second. At Schaffer collateral–CA1 synapses, with normal magnesium outside the cell, LTP is triggered by calcium entering through NMDA receptors. Substantial entry needs glutamate and enough local depolarization together.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: canonical LTP at Schaffer collateral–CA1 synapses (normal extracellular Mg2+, co-agonist present): substantial Ca2+ entry through NMDA receptors needs glutamate and sufficient local depolarization together. What sets the direction is a model.
scenes.narration: One receptor answers the first puzzle, and offers a model for the second. At Schaffer collateral–CA1 synapses, with normal magnesium outside the cell, LTP is triggered by calcium entering through NMDA receptors. Substantial entry needs glutamate and enough local depolarization together.
